clue.text: For musical event, check warning light as soon as king enters court

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check
amber is the traffic light that warns a change is coming

indicators.note: the words for as soon as and king go into the court's letters, so they enter it

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, as in 'once he arrives'
R is short for Latin rex, king

explanation.surface: A driver at a palace concert notices the dashboard light up the moment the king walks into court.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'For', read as 'giving a musical event'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber concert is a performance of small-ensemble classical music, a kind of musical event.

clue.text: Feature of architect's car I adapted

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinctive feature of a designer's vehicle that the narrator has modified.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is a distinguishing trait or quality, which is what a feature means.

clue.text: Head off prison guard covering part of wing

indicators.note: taking the head off means the first letter of the guard's title is removed

parts.note: a jailer guards a prison
on can mean covering, as in a lid on a pot

explanation.surface: A warder is decapitated while protecting part of a prison wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft's wing used to control roll.

clue.text: Their wares are bound to be ready for shelves

definitions.text: Their wares are bound to be ready for shelves

parts.words: Their wares are bound to be ready for shelves
parts.note: 'bound' means both certain and having a binding, so the wares are books, sold by the traders who stock shelves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'certain to be', but here it means books in bindings, which shops put on shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Booksellers are traders whose goods are bound volumes, displayed on shop shelving.

clue.text: Make amendments to left-wing legislation

parts.note: red is the colour of left-wing politics
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A call to revise a socialist law.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit or censor a text, making changes to it before release.

clue.text: Busy with someone inside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: engaged in activity, kept busy
second meaning: in use, as a toilet or room that has somebody in it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a busy room; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both engaged in a task and having a person present, like an engaged lavatory.

clue.text: Drink — it begins to get one down

definitions.text: it begins to get one down
definitions.meaning: second meaning: these three letters begin the answer to 1 Down, read as 'one down'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one down' sounds like depressing someone, but it refers to clue 1 Down, whose answer opens with these letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is an informal British word for tea, a common drink.

clue.text: Key Italian used in authentic musical performance

indicators.note: the key and Italian are put inside the word for authentic

parts.note: real means authentic, genuine
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A genuine concert performed in an Italian key.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert of music given by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Artisan stupidly interrupting university official, off-putting type

indicators.note: the jumbled word breaks into the official's title, interrupting it

parts.note: a proctor is a disciplinary officer at a university such as Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: done stupidly means jumbled about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy craftsman barges in on a university disciplinary officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-putting' looks like 'unpleasant', but here it means one who puts things off.
explanation.definitionFit: A procrastinator habitually delays tasks, a person who keeps postponing things.

clue.text: A couple of pounds had an effect, taking everything into account

parts.note: L is a pound, so two pounds give LL
told means had an effect, as in 'the strain told on him'

explanation.surface: Losing two pounds made a difference, when everything was considered.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning in total, with everything counted.

clue.text: Opportunist in section of church, ultimately changing side

indicators.note: the final letter, standing for one side (left), is switched for the other side (right)

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: A schemer in part of the church who finally switches allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right, the two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is an informal British term for someone who takes risks to exploit opportunities.

clue.text: Odd parts of aviary in which birds fly around

indicators.note: the odd parts are the first, third and fifth letters of the word that follows

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word for a birdhouse

explanation.surface: Some bits of an aviary where the birds fly about.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds fly through the atmosphere, the medium that surrounds and supports them in flight.

clue.text: Obsequious and silly chap isn't coy

indicators.note: silly suggests disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a foolish man who is fawning and certainly not shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophantic describes servile flattery, behaving like a toady to win favour.

clue.text: I help with a cargo at sea, for Indonesia or Philippines, say

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor offers to load freight on a voyage to South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nations are island chains, examples of a group of islands scattered across sea.

clue.text: Front of tropical fish seen in seaweed

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of tropical
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: The head of a tropical fish is spotted among the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for large brown kelp, a kind of seaweed.

clue.text: Origin of many a clue recycled every year? It's my fault

indicators.note: a word's origin is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of many

indicators.note: recycled means reprocessed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PA is short for per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A setter confesses that many clues get reused annually.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is a Latin phrase admitting personal responsibility, saying the mistake was mine.

clue.text: Again run in behind others

parts.note: rear means behind, the back part
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Running in again behind other competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrest is to take someone into custody a second time, the slang 'run in' meaning arrest.

clue.text: Attacked with missiles, alien inside was shaking

indicators.note: the alien goes inside the word for was shaking

parts.note: rocked means swayed or was shaking
ET is the film's extraterrestrial alien

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial in a craft trembled while under missile fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To rocket a place is to bombard it with rocket weapons.

clue.text: Officer I stationed in Scottish island

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the island's name, as if posted there

parts.note: Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An officer recalls being posted to a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer, ranking above a lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Dance music has very little changed in last section

indicators.note: the closing pair of letters of the word for tiny swap places

parts.note: minute means very small

explanation.surface: A dance score that barely alters in its final movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a stately triple-time dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: Perform hair-raising act, resulting in reprimand

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read whimsically: to braid hair up, raising it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair-raising' suggests something terrifying; split as UP BRAID it literally means plaiting hair upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold or criticise them sharply, which a reprimand does.

clue.text: A piece of cake is included in this — I'm pleased

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run on across these words, spanning the end of the first, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A happy baker says a slice of cake is part of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for an easy task, something straightforward.

clue.text: Way to take courses without anyone having to wait

definitions.text: Way to take courses without anyone having to wait

parts.words: Way to take courses without anyone having to wait
parts.note: the courses are courses of a meal, and to wait is to serve tables, so diners help themselves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests study and 'wait' suggests queuing, but they mean dishes and waiting at table.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-service is a system where diners collect their own food at a counter rather than being brought it by staff.

clue.text: Returned to trap outlaw

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to nab is to catch or trap

explanation.surface: A fugitive came back to catch a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to prohibit it, making it illegal.

clue.text: 70% of belongings destroyed in base

parts.note: the word has ten letters, so 70% is its first seven

clue.text: Bride and groom first of all collected some luggage

indicators.note: the first letter of each word, taken all together

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: The newlyweds pick up their suitcases before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag is a piece of luggage, such as a suitcase or holdall.

clue.text: Agricultural worker finding insect on vegetables

indicators.note: in a down clue, on would mean above, but in an across clue it means placed after

parts.note: peas are vegetables
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A farmhand discovers a bug crawling on the vegetable crop.

clue.text: Holder of evidence about crash given fine, not heavy, by judge

parts.note: light is the opposite of heavy
a recorder is a part-time judge in England and Wales
